local-development.title: Local Development Phase
bullets: Developer writes code locally using an IDE.
Local testing includes unit tests, linters (ESLint, Pylint), formatters (Prettier), type checks (TypeScript), and local builds.
If tests fail → debug & fix loop until all checks pass.
git commit saves a snapshot of changes with a message.
git push uploads local commits to the remote GitHub repository.
Pull Request (PR) is opened to propose merging changes into the main branch, triggering peer code review.

continuous-integration.title: Continuous Integration Phase
bullets: PR merge triggers the CI pipeline automatically (via GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD).
CI system runs on a remote machine/server, not your local machine.

Steps: Checkout source code → Install dependencies → Build the application → SAST (Static Application Security Testing) scans code for vulnerabilities without running it → Execute tests → Code coverage check ensures enough code is tested.
If any task fails → pipeline stops → developer fixes & pushes again.
On success → build artifact (JAR, Docker image, binary) is stored in a registry.

continuous-delivery-deployment.title: Continuous Delivery / Deployment Phase
bullets: Artifact from CI is fetched by the CD system.
Manual Approval Gate — a human reviews and approves before deployment (Continuous Delivery) or it's fully automated (Continuous Deployment).
Config & secrets (API keys, env variables) are injected at this stage, never hardcoded.
Docker image is published to Docker Hub (or ECR, GCR).
Image is pulled and deployed to a Staging Server (mirrors production environment).
Smoke tests verify basic functionality; health checks confirm the app is running.
If checks fail → developer team is notified → fixes applied → back to CD system.

production.title: Production Phase
bullets: Once all staging checks pass, deployment strategy is chosen: Blue-Green (two identical environments, switch traffic instantly), Canary (roll out to a small % of users first), Rolling (gradually replace old instances with new ones), or Recreate (shut down old, spin up new — causes downtime).
Automated or manual deployment to production.
Post-production health check confirms everything is stable after going live.
Monitoring & Observability — tools like Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog track logs, metrics, and traces continuously.
If health check fails → Rollback to last stable version immediately.
On success → End users receive the new version → Team is notified.
